title: Cell Division and Differentiation
seo_title: Mitosis Worksheets: The Cell Cycle, Phases of Mitosis and Stem Cells (Biology)
standard_text: Use a model to illustrate the role of cellular division (mitosis) and differentiation in producing and maintaining complex organisms.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on mitosis and differentiation (NGSS HS-LS1-4): the cell cycle, phases of mitosis, chromosome numbers and stem cells. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Differentiation turns them into many kinds of specialized cells.
body_html:
How to think about it

One cell → many cells → many kinds of cells.

  • Interphase: the cell grows and copies its DNA (most of the cycle).
  • Mitosis: prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase; then cytokinesis. Two identical cells, same chromosome number.
  • Differentiation: stem cells turn on different genes and become muscle, nerve or blood cells.
Example

A human cell (46 chromosomes) divides by mitosis. Daughter cells?

Mitosis keeps the number

Answer: 46 each

Example

One cell divides 5 times. How many cells?

2^5

Answer: 32

Common mistakes

  • Thinking mitosis halves the chromosome number. Meiosis does that.
  • Thinking a cell spends most of its time dividing. Most time is interphase.
  • Thinking different cell types have different DNA. They use different genes.

faq.q: What are the phases of mitosis?
faq.a: Prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase, followed by cytokinesis. Before mitosis, the cell copies its DNA in interphase.

faq.q: How many chromosomes do daughter cells have?
faq.a: The same number as the parent cell. A human cell with 46 chromosomes makes two cells with 46 each.

faq.q: How do cells become different if they have the same DNA?
faq.a: During differentiation, each cell type turns on different genes.

items.q: Which stage is this? DNA is replicated during the S stage.
items.e: Interphase: DNA is replicated during the S stage.

items.q: Do a muscle cell and a nerve cell in the same person have the same DNA?
c: Yes, but they use different genes.
items.e: Gene expression differs.

items.q: Which stage is this? The cell grows and copies its DNA.
items.e: Interphase: The cell grows and copies its DNA.

items.q: Why do multicellular organisms need mitosis?
c: for growth and to repair or replace cells
items.e: More cells for growth and repair.

items.q: Which stage comes right after anaphase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: Which stage comes right before telophase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: Which stage is this? Chromosomes condense and become visible; the nuclear membrane breaks down.

items.q: What does mitosis produce?
c: two cells with half the DNA
items.e: Same chromosome number.

items.q: Which stage comes right before anaphase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: What is differentiation?
c: cells becoming specialized for different jobs
items.e: Same DNA, different genes on.

items.q: Which stage is this? The cell looks pinched in the middle as it splits in two.
items.e: Cytokinesis: The cell looks pinched in the middle as it splits in two.

items.q: Which stage comes right after telophase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: What is a stem cell?
c: an unspecialized cell that can become different cell types
a cell in a plant stem only
items.e: It can differentiate.

items.q: Which stage is this? The chromosomes start to uncoil as new nuclear membranes appear.

items.q: Which stage comes right after interphase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: What structure pulls chromosomes apart?
items.e: Spindles attach at centromeres.

items.q: Which stage is this? Sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite ends of the cell.
items.e: Anaphase: Sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite ends of the cell.

items.q: What can happen when the cell cycle is not controlled?
c: cells divide too much and can form a tumor (cancer)
items.e: Cancer is uncontrolled division.

items.q: During which stage is DNA copied?
items.e: Before mitosis begins.

items.q: Which stage is this? Spindle fibers attach to the centromeres at the cell's middle line.
